does: Cooks a browned joint slowly in milk in a covered pot, so that the meat turns tender and the milk splits and reduces into golden, nutty curds that become the sauce.

intro.what: Milk is the braising liquid and splits on purpose.
intro.why: The lemon and the long heat split the milk; its sugars brown into a nutty sauce while the gentle heat keeps lean pork moist.

how: Brown the meat well in butter and pour off most of the fat.
Add aromatics such as garlic, sage and strips of lemon peel, then warm milk to come about half way up the meat.
Bring it to a bare simmer, set the lid ajar and cook very gently, turning the meat now and then.
When the meat is tender and the milk has split into golden curds, lift the meat out and boil the curds down until brown.

cues.text: The milk splits into small golden-brown curds in a little fat.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling the milk hard, so it catches and burns on the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Keep it at a bare simmer and scrape the bottom now and then.

mistakes.mistake: Thinking the split milk has gone wrong and throwing it away.
mistakes.fix: The curds are the point: brown them and serve them as the sauce.

quiz.question: What happens to the milk as it cooks?
choices: It splits into curds that brown into the sauce.
It is drained off and thrown away.

quiz.question: How hard should the pot bubble?
quiz.because: Gentle heat stops the milk catching.

quiz.question: What should the finished sauce look like?
choices: Golden-brown curds in a little fat.

quiz.question: The milk caught and burned on the bottom. What would you change?
choices: Keep it at a bare simmer and scrape the bottom now and then.
Boil it harder at the start.
quiz.because: Low heat and scraping prevent burning.

comes_after.why: The meat is browned before the milk goes in.

variant_of.differs: The liquid is milk, which splits and browns into curds that become the sauce; the meat is a leaner joint, cooked gently with the lid ajar.
